title: Plan de acción para la implementación de estrategias ante el desabastecimiento del sistema de saneamiento básico como factor contribuyente a las infecciones diarreicas agudas en niños menores de 5 años en Secocha, 2025
rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). This 2025 postgraduate 'Trabajo Académico' is a public-health Action Plan ('Plan de acción') proposing community hygiene promotion, dry/ecological latrine installation, and local monitoring to reduce acute diarrheal infections in children under 5 in Secocha, Peru. Despite mentioning a 120-household sample and interviews in the abstract and methods, the full text reports zero primary empirical data, zero survey statistics, and zero qualitative interview findings (Table 3 describes planned analyses in the future tense, Annexes 1-5 provide blank instruments, and Chapter IV presents implementation schedules and projected targets). Additionally, it fails Criterion 2 because it examines generic community health promotion, basic sanitation project delivery, and unanalysed institutional background rather than any rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism governing service access.

title: O direito humano de acesso à água potável: uma análise continental baseada nos Fóruns Mundiais da Água/The human right of access to drinking water: a continental analysis based on World Water Forums
rationale: Excluded as E05 (no empirical evidence on service access). Full-text Portuguese article matches the record metadata (Zorzi, Turatti, & Mazzarino, 2016, doi:10.4136/ambi-agua.1861). The paper conducts a qualitative textual summary and keyword search ('human right' / 'human rights') of final reports and website pages from the 1st through 6th World Water Forums (1997–2012) to trace international and continental diplomatic discourse on the human right to drinking water. It contains no primary or secondary empirical evidence on household or community water or sanitation service access (failing C1 and C3), analyzes macro-level international summit rhetoric rather than a rule-type legal/administrative mechanism governing access under the 2026-10-13 C2 clarification (though it passes the plain broad wording of C2), and reports only summit declaration themes, participant totals, and keyword shares rather than any real-world service-access outcome (failing C4 and C5; hence excluded under both plain and narrow C2 readings).

title: Racializing the (Sociological) view on environmental health in the sanitation of the black population: A colonial continuum called environmental racism; [Racializando o olhar (Sociológico) sobre a saúde ambiental em saneamento da população negra: Um continuum colonial chamado racismo ambiental]
rationale: reason: "full text not accessible". Retrieval status is not_accessible and no full-text PDF, OA XML or abstract text was provided in the screening packet. Per protocol rules, eligibility across Criteria 1-6 (under both the plain wording and the 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2) cannot be guessed from title/metadata alone, requiring decision "cannot_tell" and exclusion_code "NONE".

title: South Africa's new water policy: Towards environmental management of resources?; [La nouvelle politique de l'eau en Afrique du Sud: Vers une gestion environnementale des ressources?]
rationale: Exclude as E01 (Wrong topic — water-resource and fluvial environmental management study unrelated to household or community water/sanitation service access, per Exclusion Criterion 7). While Blanchon (2003) briefly notes apartheid-era inequalities in potable water access and the 25 L/person/day basic human needs component of the statutory Reserve as background to South Africa's 1998 National Water Act, the paper explicitly sets aside the human Reserve calculation and examines the hydrological, ecological, and bulk basin-allocation challenges of defining and enforcing the environmental Reserve in the Orange River basin. It neither analyzes a rule-type mechanism governing household/community service access (failing narrow Criterion 2) nor reports any household or community service access outcome (failing Criteria 1 and 4; thus also excluded under the plain Criterion 2 reading).

title: Análisis de eficiencia de empresas de servicios públicos de agua potable y saneamiento en Perú: una aproximación DEA en dos etapas
rationale: Excluded under E04 (Wrong outcome). Although this empirical Master's thesis (in Spanish, with full text directly readable) evaluates regulatory interventions in Peru's urban water and sanitation sector—specifically SUNASS tariff regulation duration, tariff formula transition length, supervisory inspections (fiscalizaciones), and OTASS Transitional Support Regime (RAT) intervention—its dependent variable is exclusively utility-level input-oriented DEA technical efficiency (te_vrs), measuring radial reduction in utility inputs (workers, operating costs, water produced, pipe network length) holding outputs fixed. Service indicators such as active water connections and continuity are used only as exogenous demand-determined outputs inside the first-stage DEA efficiency score and are not modeled as access, connection, continuity, or affordability outcomes of legal or regulatory rules. Accordingly, it fails Criteria 1 and 4 (and fails narrow Criterion 2 because the regulatory variables are not studied as rule-type mechanisms governing household/community service access), yielding exclusion under both the narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings.

title: From the Paramos to the City: Environmental History, Water Sources, and More-Than-Human Governance for the City of Quito, Ecuador; [Dos páramos à cidade: história ambiental, fontes de água e governança mais que humana para a cidade de Quito, Equador]; [De los páramos a la urbe: historia ambiental, fuentes de agua y gobernanza más que humana para la ciudad de Quito, Ecuador]
rationale: Excluded as E05 (No empirical evidence). This 21-page Spanish-language article is a narrative historiographical review and conceptual essay ('revisión historiográfica') based on secondary literature and published statutes, with no primary empirical data or systematic synthesis method. Substantively, it also falls outside the review's scope (failing c1, narrow c2, c4, and c5) because it examines macro-level bulk water source expansion, upstream páramo conservation, and watershed trust-fund governance (FONAG) for a 'more-than-human' environmental history of Quito rather than rule-type mechanisms governing household or community water or sanitation service access or empirical service-access outcomes.

title: WATER SUPPLY IN COLONIAL SANTIAGO: INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK AND GOVERNANCE; [EL ABASTECIMIENTO DE AGUA EN EL SANTIAGO COLONIAL: INSTITUCIONALIDAD Y GOBERNANZA]
rationale: This Spanish-language article is a narrative administrative and historical overview of urban drinking water supply in colonial Santiago de Chile (1541-1810) based entirely on secondary historical literature, with no empirical methods, no primary archival or empirical data, and no systematic empirical synthesis (E05). In addition, while it satisfies the plain wording of Criterion 2 by discussing colonial governance institutions, it focuses on macro-historical institutional jurisdiction and public-works financing rather than analysing a specific rule-type mechanism governing household service access under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading; under both readings of Criterion 2, it is excluded for lack of empirical evidence.

title: Environmental sanitation in São Paulo Macrometropolis: perspectives for a multilevel governance; [Saneamento ambiental na Macrometrópole Paulista: perspectivas para uma governança multinível]; [Saneamiento Ambiental en la Macrometrópolis Paulista: perspectivas para la Gobernanza Multinivel]
rationale: Excluded primarily under E03 (Wrong exposure): under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, the paper examines macro-level multi-level governance architecture, federative competence sharing, municipal sanitation plan adoption, collaborative urban stream depollution (Córrego Limpo), and watershed committee negotiations over bulk raw-water abstraction permits (Cantareira System), rather than a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access. Furthermore, even under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2 (plain_criterion2_decision = 'exclude'), the paper remains ineligible because aggregate SNIS 2018 water and sewage coverage figures (Table 1) are presented only as static problem-framing background and are never analyzed in relation to any governance factor, while the study's evaluated outcomes (Chart 2, Figure 2) are governance process characteristics (horizontal/vertical integration, citizen participation, territoriality, and municipal planning) synthesized from official documents and secondary academic literature (c4 = no, c5 = no).

title: Optimal water tariffs and trade-offs: a multi-objective analysis of municipalities in Pernambuco; [Tarifas ótimas de água e compensações: uma análise multiobjetivo dos municípios de Pernambuco]
rationale: This English-language empirical and calibrated multi-objective optimization study examines potable water tariff and cost-recovery rules across 172 municipalities in Pernambuco, Brazil (1,805,405 active COMPESA connections) using 2010 SINISA, COMPESA administrative records, and IBGE Census household income data. It directly evaluates tariff and cost-recovery rules—including social residential (<1 minimum wage) versus non-social residential tariff differentiation—which is an explicitly listed rule-type mechanism under both the plain wording and the 2026-10-13 narrow clarification of Criterion 2. It reports both observed 2010 and Pareto-optimal outcomes for household water affordability (relative to the 3%-of-income benchmark, including the number of municipalities exceeding the threshold) and water quantity demanded, satisfying all systematic-review inclusion criteria (c1–c6).

title: Human rights in Spain: Protection of the right to water in families with affordability problems. Critical analysis for legal reform; [Derechos humanos en España: Protección del derecho al agua en familias con problemas de asequibilidad por riesgo de pobreza y exclusión social. Análisis crítico para una reforma legal]
rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). While the paper squarely addresses household drinking-water affordability and disconnections (c1) and analyzes specific statutory and municipal rule-type mechanisms governing tariff discounts, social funds, eligibility screening, and disconnection prohibitions (c2, satisfying both plain and narrow 2026-10-13 readings), it is explicitly a critical normative legal essay ('ensayo ... desde una perspectiva normativa') proposing legal reform. It presents no primary empirical data, no qualitative or quantitative empirical methods, and no systematic empirical synthesis, relying only on doctrinal analysis of legal texts and narrative citation of secondary industry reports.

title: Expresión de emociones ante la dificultad de acceso al agua: un estudio de caso en la Cuenca del alto Lerma.
rationale: Excluded as E04 (Wrong outcome), with concurrent failure of Criterion 2 under the 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading. Rather than examining how a legal, administrative, or regulatory rule governs household water access, this Spanish-language case study in San Pedro Tultepec (Lerma, Mexico) reverses the causal direction and studies how household water scarcity, reliance on tanker trucks (pipas), and living near wetlands and an inter-basin water transfer system supplying Mexico City affect residents' subjective emotions (anger, sadness, indifference, joy) and emotional motivation to protest. No empirical household service-access outcome is evaluated for the study site (only national INEGI 2020 census figures are cited as background), and public water-transfer policy appears only as macro-governance context (with a single unanalysed observation that residents fill out forms at the local delegation to request tanker trucks). Consequently, the study is excluded under both the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading and the plain wording of Criterion 2.

title: Rehablitation of water networks : Decision making processes of the Care-W Project; [Réhabilitation des réseaux d'eau potable : Les processus de décision et le projet CARE-W]
rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic). Based on the retrieved 2005 English full text in Water Science & Technology: Water Supply by the same four authors reporting the CARE-W WP3 study (noting the metadata carries a bilingual English/French variant title and swaps the 2nd and 3rd authors), the paper investigates internal water utility decision-making processes for physical pipe network rehabilitation (long-term planning, annual programming, urgent pipe interventions, budgeting, and road-works coordination) to design a computer-aided decision support system (CARE-W) across 14 European utilities. It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (failing c1), does not analyse a rule-type legal/administrative mechanism governing service access under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 scope (failing c2), and reports no service access, connection, continuity, reliability, or affordability outcomes (failing c4). Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the decision would still be 'exclude' due to failing Criteria 1 and 4.

title: Water for everybody?; [De l'eau pour tous?]
rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). Although the article topically addresses water and sanitation access in low-income urban settlements (c1) and rule-type legal/institutional/contractual mechanisms such as concession contract rules, municipal refusal to recognize illegal land occupation via service provision, social tariffs, and prepayment (c2 under both plain and narrow readings), it is a brief practitioner/corporate overview summarizing an internal Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux working group reflection and book, with no empirical data, sample, research methods, or measured access outcomes.

title: Factors for the Decision to Drink Tap Water in Three Metropolitan Areas of Mexico; [Factores en la decisión de beber agua directamente de la red pública en tres Zonas Metropolitanas de México]
rationale: Excluded under E03 (wrong exposure; also fails c1 and c4). Using a 2018 survey of 1,800 connected urban dwellings in three Mexican municipalities, Aguilar-Benitez (2024) estimates a recursive bivariate probit model of households' behavioural decision to drink tap water directly from the public network and their subjective satisfaction with water service. No legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor is empirically examined under either the plain wording of Criterion 2 or the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading: official water-quality standards are mentioned only in background context and effective regulation is raised only as a concluding policy recommendation, whereas the actual explanatory variables are perceived water purity, past waterborne illness, operational continuity and pressure, household sociodemographic traits, and municipal dummies. Moreover, surveyed households already have piped water access and the modelled outcomes are consumer tap-water drinking behaviour and satisfaction rather than service access or connection.

title: impacto agua Transformations of the Urban-Rural Space in Colombia and Their Impact on Water Supply
rationale: This Spanish-language socio-legal empirical article (from the Universidad Nacional de Colombia project 'Agua y buen vivir, las organizaciones comunitarias y la normatividad en Colombia') examines rural and peri-urban water service access in Colombia through document/registry analysis and participatory fieldwork (8 workshops/forums and field observations with second-tier community aqueduct associations). Although framed broadly around urban-rural territorial transformations, it directly examines rule-type legal and administrative mechanisms governing service access under both the plain and narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 readings—including statutory urban-rural classifications and POT land-use enforcement, differential service regulations (esquemas diferenciales), administrative/technical/digital compliance burdens and selective enforcement deterring community aqueduct formalization in RUPS, mandatory micrometering, water permitting, and flat community tariff quotas—and links them to water coverage, formalization, service continuity, and sufficiency outcomes. Eligible as a qualitative socio-legal study for mechanism synthesis, with Spanish translation feasible from full text per Criterion 10.
